text:
ANTHROPIC'S IPO DOCUMENTS ARE CALMING DOWN THE MARKETS.

None of the numbers released today are that different from what we heard last week, but now we know how much cash they have. 

Anthropic has $120B in cash and is likely raising $100B on the IPO. They are then likely going to be raising another $100B in debt, $60B of it already financed by BlackStone. If you assume a 3x in ARR, which probably is low considering how much the street wants them to grow, this company should have around $300-$400B in cash. This also doesn't take into account the future ATMs they might engage in.

So, the reason AI stocks are getting some relief right now is because it seems like Anthropic will have enough cash to pay their bills, which obviously is good for $NVDA, $SPCX, $AMD, $AVGO, $MU, and many other players. 

However, there are going to be 24 separate unlocks in 2027. Those are going to be days where the market has to deal with a massive amount of supply coming onto the market. The company effectively has unilateral control, not shareholders, on deciding to pause or slow down the release of models. The open-weight models continue to be a threat as more enterprises are seeing the value in owning their AI for a significantly cheaper cost. Anthropic has outlined all these risks in the S1.

Regardless on if you are buying the IPO, it seems like there is enough cash they can raise to continue paying their bills and making sure the downstream value flows into most of the semis...if the market

en_summary: (Reposted by @TheStalwart) @aRishisays explains why the Brazil election shock felt extraordinary: vital elections are rare when politics has centrist continuity, and upsets usually come from 60/40 setups, not 80/20; it is a binary, non reflexive event unlike the FOMC.
text:
Two reasons:

1. Elections that are this vital have usually been rare (getting more frequent now - think France, US, Canada last year, Brazil today). Most of the time elections don’t matter much for markets when there is some kind of centrist continuity to politics. 

2. When they do matter, upsets happen but typically from a 60-40, 66-33 setup instead of 80-20. 

Combined, this Brazil election becomes a huge surprise and hence feels extraordinary. But then again, it’s a binary, non-reflexive event (unlike the FOMC) so the odds don’t really have predictive power. It’s just a collective guess, and so expected to miss every now and then.

text:
The Fed is expected to hold rates steady Wednesday, but it is a closer call on the data than the market-implied probabilities suggest.

The case for hiking: 
1) The hot September CPI and PPI underscore a second straight lost year for getting inflation down
2) With a Dec hike widely expected, hawks will argue that there's less to gain from waiting six weeks given the cost of falling further behind
3) Hawks will also argue that policy isn't restrictive and needs to be

The case for holding:
1) If officials still think this is a 2-3 hike recalibration, spacing out remaining moves costs little. "Being six weeks late is a manageable risk," says Rob Kaplan

text:
SpaceX has officially announced that they have secured $40 billion in the largest GPU financing ever.

The company entered into a $40B master finance lease for GPUs and related equipment with an entity managed by Apollo Global Management. This lease will deliver the next generation of NVIDIA Vera Rubin chips for SpaceX's terrestrial compute buildout and is an important step in our plan to build a Super Intelligence future. It represents the largest committed GPU financing ever.

SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen:
"SpaceX aims to deploy the largest compute infrastructure in the world. As demand for compute continues to accelerate, we're seeing less than one year payback periods on our SI infrastructure investments. This lease diversifies our funding sources and addresses a notable portion of the funding required to deliver on our growth plans as we aim to get additional compute online at record speeds to power Grok for enterprises and consumers, as well as serve existing and future cloud services customers."

Transaction Details:
The financing has been committed to by a number of financing parties led by Apollo and Goldman Sachs, who served as sole structuring agent. Entry into the lease remains subject to certain specified closing conditions and is expected to close prior to year-end 2026, with lease schedules expected to commence upon delivery of GPUs and related equipment in the first half of 2027.

text:
$META

META OFFICIALLY ENTERS THE CAPITAL RAISING GAME THROUGH SELLING MORE OF THEIR STOCK.

Meta announced plans to raise approximately $35 billion through two equity offerings:

- $22.5B in Class A common stock through forward sale agreements.

- $12.5B in depositary shares tied to mandatory convertible preferred stock.

The company is also considering a separate $60 billion offering program for its new nonvoting Class C shares, potentially beginning in Q1 2027. The nonvoting class was introduced on earnings last week and will result in a 2-for-1 stock split. 

The total raise so far will be around $95B, $10B more than Google’s $85B equity offering from a few months ago. 

$NVDA NVIDIA, $AMD, and $AVGO Broadcom have also expressed nonbinding interest in purchasing a combined $5 billion of Meta shares…which basically means the suppliers of chips to Meta will now be taking a direct equity stake into them. Meta already has warrants that convert into shares for 10% of $AMD if it holds above $600 in the future. 

Capital is now becoming the constraint…whoever can raise the most will win.

Every dollar wants to be in AI compute right now

ARK Invest's Brett Winton on why that's making Bitcoin's "insurance" more expensive to hold

"Right now the world is basically sending out this giant emergency spinning beacon. All capital available needs to go into AI compute infrastructure, because we need as much as possible."

"Any asset that's not generating immediate great returns looks net worse on that basis. And so the cost of holding Bitcoin for this insurance contract has gone up."

"It's not just a Bitcoin and cryptocurrency issue. That is an issue for all businesses of all stripes all over the world."

"There's a black hole, and there's kind of like the tidal force that's pulling money into creating the infrastructure we need for superintelligence."
